# Awesome Generalist Robotics

![Awesome Generalist Robotics — shared competence, diverse embodiments](assets/banner.svg)

**A curated research collection on generalist robot policies, cross-embodiment learning, and unified embodied autonomy.**

How can robots reuse learned competence across tasks, environments, sensors, and physical bodies? This collection brings together research on shared policies, reusable representations, morphology-aware control, world models, and integrated autonomy systems, alongside datasets and benchmarks needed to evaluate them. It spans manipulation, navigation, locomotion, and multiple robot morphologies, connecting advances in robot foundation models with the physical constraints and deployment demands of autonomous systems.

[Website](https://ntnu-arl.github.io/awesome-generalist-robotics/) · Last curated: 2026-11-06 · [Compact index](docs/by-year.md) · [Scope and curation](docs/curation.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## How to read this list

References are organized by **year, newest first**, and alphabetically by title within each year. Each entry has a primary-source link, year, resource type, and a very short account of its contribution. Years usually identify the first arXiv release, otherwise they follow the linked publication record.

## Contributing

Suggestions, metadata corrections, and evidence-based scope clarifications are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), edit the [catalogue](data/catalog.json), and regenerate the lists. Use the issue forms if you prefer to suggest a reference without editing files.

## Curation and acknowledgements

This is a selective reading list, not a systematic review or a leaderboard. Summaries describe research contributions; inclusion is not endorsement or independent replication. See the [curation notes](docs/curation.md) for coverage and verification limits.

The initial collection combines an existing robotics literature map with reference discovery through [Awesome Generalist Agents](https://github.com/cheryyunl/awesome-generalist-agents). Research credit belongs to the authors of the linked works. Please cite the original papers for scientific claims.
